concepts.def: Made of simple sugars such as glucose; the main energy source.
Made of amino acids; used for growth, repair and to build enzymes.
Fats and oils used as an energy store and for insulation.
Protein catalysts with a specific active site (lock and key).
High temperature or the wrong pH changes the active site so the enzyme stops working.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Biological Molecules — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Biological Molecules brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Biological Molecules.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right?
options: It must pump blood at high pressure around the whole body; the right ventricle only pumps to the nearby lungs.
The left ventricle is thicker because it handles oxygenated blood, which is harder to pump.
Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.
The left ventricle is thicker because it is on the same side as the brain.

mcqs.q: Why are food chains usually limited to about 4 or 5 trophic levels?
options: Only ~10 percent of energy is transferred between trophic levels; eventually too little energy remains to support another level.
Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.
There aren't enough types of animals to fill more trophic levels.
The left ventricle is thicker because it is on the same side as the brain.

mcqs.q: What is the main role of mitochondria in a cell?
options: The left ventricle is thicker because it is on the same side as the brain.
Mitochondria store sunlight and release it for photosynthesis.
Mitochondria produce energy by creating it from nothing.
To carry out aerobic respiration, producing ATP that cells use as an energy currency.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ester bond”?
options: Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hydrolysis”?
options: Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Glycosidic bond”?
options: Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Polymer”?
options: Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Monomer”?
options: Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Condensation reaction”?
options: Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.

mcqs.q: A student adds Benedict's solution to a sugar solution and heats it; it turns brick-red. Which conclusion is supported?
options: A reducing sugar is present.
Starch is present.
Protein is present.
Lipid is present.

mcqs.q: A food sample turns the biuret reagent purple. This shows the sample contains:
options: Protein
Reducing sugar
Starch
Fat

mcqs.q: Two amino acids join during protein synthesis. What type of reaction occurs and what is released?
options: Condensation, releasing water
Hydrolysis, taking in water
Condensation, releasing carbon dioxide
Oxidation, releasing oxygen

mcqs.q: A student tests a sample with iodine solution and it turns blue-black. Which molecule is present?
options: Starch
Glucose
Protein
A lipid

free_texts.q: Type the key term that means: "Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions."
free_texts.hint: It's one of the six key terms above.

sequence.def: Monomers; the building blocks of all proteins
Condensation joins amino acids, releasing water
The sequence of amino acids in the chain
Local folding into alpha-helices and beta-sheets
Overall 3-D shape held by R-group bonds
Two or more chains combine, e.g. haemoglobin
